Cloning https://aur.archlinux.org/xcaddy.git...

Analyzing xcaddy AUR package with qwen/qwen3-235b-a22b-2507
Performing initial audit of PKGBUILD to ensure that we can safely run `makepkg`
LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD defines standard sources using a git clone from the declared upstream URL, specifically `git+https://github.com/caddyserver/xcaddy.git#tag=v0.4.7`. The `sha512sums` array is set to 'SKIP', which is common and acceptable for VCS sources in AUR packages, especially when the source is a git repository. During `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare`, the source will be cloned but not built or prepared, meaning no build or package functions are executed.

Top-level code in the PKGBUILD is minimal and consists only of variable assignments. There is no command substitution, no remote code execution, and no network activity beyond cloning the declared upstream source. The `pkgver()` function is not defined, so version computation is not dynamic. As such, sourcing this PKGBUILD does not trigger any unexpected or dangerous behavior.

The use of `--noprepare` ensures that even if the git repository contained malicious prepare() logic, it would not be executed at this stage. The commands `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` and `makepkg --printsrcinfo` will only parse the PKGBUILD and fetch sources, which is safe in this context.
</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>
<summary>
No malicious code execution during source fetch and parse
</summary>
</security_assessment>

<details>
The provided `.SRCINFO` file is a metadata file used by Arch Linux's AUR to describe the package build configuration. It specifies that the package `xcaddy` is built from a Git source at `https://github.com/caddyserver/xcaddy.git`, specifically checking out the tag `v0.4.7`. This aligns with standard AUR packaging practices for versioned releases.

The `sha512sums = SKIP` entry is expected for VCS sources like git, as the actual content of the repository at build time may vary (e.g., due to shallow clones or branch updates), and full reproducibility depends on the integrity of the tagged commit in the upstream repository. Skipping checksums in such cases is common and not inherently unsafe, especially when a specific tag is referenced.

There are no network operations, file modifications, or executable commands in this file. It contains only declarative metadata about the package: description, version, architecture, dependencies, source location, and checksum policy. No malicious behavior—such as code injection, data exfiltration, or unauthorized downloads—is possible from this file alone.
</details>

The build() function sets standard Go environment variables and compiles the binary using `go build` with secure flags such as `-buildmode=pie` and `-trimpath`, which are good practices. The package() function installs the resulting binary to `/usr/bin/xcaddy` with appropriate permissions. All operations are confined to the build directory and standard packaging paths.

There are no suspicious network requests, obfuscated commands, or unauthorized file operations. The script does not execute arbitrary code from external sources, nor does it exfiltrate data. All dependencies and tools used (go, git) are expected for building a Go application from source. The package follows typical AUR packaging conventions and shows no signs of tampering or malicious behavior.
